source: Adapted from eraser_v03 development cases, including user-supplied expanded solution; suggested labels are not human gold.
opening:
An eraser is, of course, a piece of stationery used to erase something that has been written.
However, A picked up an eraser in order to leave a message on a blank sheet of paper on which nothing had yet been written.
Why?
solution: A had a mechanical pencil with no usable lead. The eraser covered the lead-refill opening, so A picked up/removed the eraser, inserted new lead, then used the pencil to write the message on the blank sheet.
canonical_facts: The pencil had no usable lead.
The eraser covered the lead-refill opening.
A removed the eraser, inserted lead, and then wrote with the pencil.
explicit_negatives: The eraser was not being used as an erasing or marking tool in this explanation.
Removing the eraser opened the refill access; it did not directly expose or extend the writing tip.
unknown_details: The eraser colour, pencil brand and exact loading hardware beyond the covered refill opening are unspecified.

host_examples.question: Did A use the eraser to remove a substance from the blank sheet?
host_examples.rationale: It was removed to load lead, not used to erase the sheet.

host_examples.question: Did A use the eraser to make visible marks on the sheet?
host_examples.rationale: Mark-making was done by the pencil, not the eraser.

host_examples.question: Was the eraser attached to the pencil that A used?
host_examples.rationale: In the ordinary sense it was the removable eraser covering that pencil's refill opening; permanent attachment is not implied.

host_examples.question: Did A use the eraser to correct a mistake made while writing the message in pencil?
host_examples.rationale: Wrong explanatory role for the eraser in this incident.

host_examples.question: Did A intend to erase any pencil marks?
host_examples.rationale: Read in the incident's context: the stated purpose was loading lead. This does not rule out every future erasing intention.

host_examples.question: Did A erase pencil marks to form the letters of the message?
host_examples.rationale: Alternative mark-forming mechanism is not the intended story.

host_examples.question: Was the eraser used for its usual purpose of removing pencil marks?
host_examples.rationale: Same purpose judgement as the earlier erasing questions.

host_examples.question: Was the pencil broken or unusable for ordinary writing?
host_examples.rationale: Read as an inclusive disjunction: no usable lead establishes unusable at that moment; mechanical damage is not required.

host_examples.question: Was the pencil tip broken?
host_examples.rationale: No usable lead does not establish why it was unusable. v0.3 uses yes and no for this unresolved or ambiguous case, without asserting partial truth.

host_examples.question: When A picked up the eraser end, did that action cause the writing end to become exposed or accessible?
host_examples.rationale: Under the direct-effect reading, it exposed refill access, not the writing end. If accessible means indirectly made usable after refilling, reword first.

host_examples.question: Was the tool inserted into or resting in some holder/container, so that grabbing the eraser end and pulling it out exposed the writing end?
host_examples.rationale: The proposed holder-based exposure mechanism replaces the stated refill mechanism.

host_examples.question: Did gravity play a role—i.e., by lifting the object from the eraser end, the writing end moved, dropped, or unfolded into an exposed position?
host_examples.rationale: Reject the specified gravity-driven tip-exposure mechanism, not every possible role of gravity while handling lead.

host_examples.question: Did the eraser end move relative to the rest of the tool when A picked it up, and that movement mechanically exposed the writing tip?
host_examples.rationale: This bundled wording asserts both relative eraser movement (true) and direct tip exposure (false). A single question asking only whether removal directly exposed the tip would be no.

host_examples.question: Did “picked up the eraser” mean that A removed/detached the eraser from the rest of the tool, rather than lifting the whole object?
host_examples.rationale: Correct contextual meaning of the action.

host_examples.question: After A removed the eraser, did that reveal a hidden button or mechanism that A then used to extend the writing tip?
host_examples.rationale: Button/extension mechanism suggests direct actuation, whereas mechanism might loosely include refill access. These readings change the answer; distinguish refilling from extending. A specific hidden button claim alone is yes and no unless excluded by additional facts. v0.3 uses yes and no for this unresolved or ambiguous case, without asserting partial truth.

host_examples.question: Did removing the eraser expose an opening where A could insert/refill pencil lead, after which A used the pencil to write the message?
host_examples.rationale: Entire described sequence matches the expanded story.

host_examples.question: Was A using a mechanical pencil, and they removed the eraser because the lead-refill opening was underneath it, inserted new lead, then used the pencil to write the message on the blank paper?
host_examples.rationale: Complete coherent explanation; no automatic rejection for multiple clauses.

host_examples.question: Did A remove the eraser and then use that eraser as a stamp to print the message?
host_examples.rationale: Removal is true; eraser-stamp use is false.

host_examples.question: Did A remove a blue eraser to refill the pencil?
host_examples.rationale: Correct purpose with an unknown colour does not qualify as mixed true/false. v0.3 uses yes and no for this unresolved or ambiguous case, without asserting partial truth.

host_examples.question: Did removing the eraser directly extend the pencil tip?
host_examples.rationale: The direct effect was opening refill access.
